author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Tesla plans to introduce its long-delayed Semi electric truck to the European market, expanding beyond North America as established manufacturers already sell battery-powered heavy trucks there. The company said it will release European specifications and launch details at the IAA Transportation trade fair in Hanover, Germany, next week.

Tesla unveiled the Semi in 2017 and originally targeted production for 2019. Limited U.S. deliveries began in late 2022 to customers including PepsiCo. In April, Tesla said the first Semi had rolled off a high-volume production line in Nevada, but a July shareholder update said production would begin in 2026 and removed an earlier forecast for volume production this year.

Tesla's German website lists a European version with up to 550 kilometers, or 342 miles, of range at a gross combination weight of 40 tonnes. The company says the truck can recover about 60% of its range in 30 minutes through its Megacharger network. The European debut will test whether Tesla can turn years of technical demonstrations into fleet-scale sales while meeting regional weight, charging and service requirements.
dek: Tesla says it will reveal European specifications and launch details for its electric heavy truck at next week's IAA Transportation show.
headline: Tesla prepares European launch details for long-delayed Semi truck
